acceptance: The cause of the SF 0.1 failure is recorded with the server and client output.
Either LakeSail completes TPC-DS-OBT at SF 0.1 and the bundle is published, or the limit is registered with the reason.
context: Filed 2026-11-11 from the benchmark scale-factor audit and the TPC-DS-OBT publication work of 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11: identified during that work and not addressed.
description:
## Problem
In the UAT sweep of 2026-11-11 that produced the published TPC-DS-OBT results, LakeSail passed SF 0.01 and failed SF 0.1 after about 20 minutes. The original error was not recorded because the harness runs the benchmark with `--quiet`. A diagnostic re-run reported 'Cannot connect to LakeSail Sail at sc://localhost:50051', which may be a consequence (the server had gone) rather than the cause. As a result the published SF 0.1 cohort has three platforms and no LakeSail result. Versions: PySail 0.7.1, PySpark client 4.2.0. Local run outputs for that sweep have been deleted.

## Change
Re-run LakeSail TPC-DS-OBT at SF 0.1 through the UAT entry point with output kept, and determine whether the server crashed (memory, timeout) or the load or a query failed. Fix or register the limit. If it then passes all 93 statements, stage and publish the bundle so the SF 0.1 cohort has four platforms.

## Guardrails
- Heavy work only through the UAT entry point or `make heavy-run`.
- Publish only a run with zero failed statements and validation passed, staged with `make corpus-stage-local`.
